#+title: Durable preparation jobs

* Ordinary operation
Build, native preparation and SDK-family production use the same fixed job path.
The managed environment selects BL_PREPARATION_COORDINATOR and Nix's build
station once; ordinary build/self-build commands need no routing flags.

The coordinator accepts immutable native, application and sdk operation data.
Nix owns realization and shares identical derivations. The pinned Foundry
mechanism maintains durable observations. Each requester owns a private request
directory and independent input/result roots. Product verification and the
existing output writer claim govern publication; job receipts grant no execution
authority.

Synchronous commands use =artifact-jobs/prepare!= to submit and wait in one
coordinator VM. The same call reconciles a safely queued worker. Its result
includes the durable handle; a deadline or disconnect leaves accepted work and
its roots available for reconnection.

* Observe and reconnect
Programmatic clients use artifact-jobs. Save the returned handle with the
request's records:

#+begin_src clojure
(ns example.preparation (:require [artifact-jobs :as jobs]))

(def handle
  (jobs/submit! pinned-coordinator private-request-directory
    {"version" 1 "kind" "native" "request" immutable-native-request}))
(jobs/status! handle)
(jobs/events! handle 0 200)
(jobs/await! handle 60000)
#+end_src

For an existing ordinary preparation, load its persisted handle rather than
submitting a new directory:

#+begin_src clojure
(let [saved (Jason/decode! (File/read! "/absolute/request-directory/handle.json"))]
  (jobs/status! saved)
  (jobs/events! saved 0 200)
  (jobs/await! saved 60000))
#+end_src

Native/application request directories live under
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/beam_lisp/artifacts (or ~/.cache/beam_lisp/artifacts). Successful
receipt records include the job handle. Calls interrupted after admission retain
handle.json and operation.json in their private request directory; interruption
earlier in capture may leave only the available input/root records. Checkout SDK jobs live
under .bl/sdks/<fingerprint>/job-*, with active-job identifying the reconnectable
attempt. Keep the request directory at its original path: handles bind both
path and directory identity. Job controls are library APIs; the artifacts CLI
lists receipts but has no job-status/cancel/recover subcommands.

The coordinator address comes from pinned startup configuration. Requests carry
fixed data schemas, never commands, tool paths, environment maps, Nix expressions
or execution grants. The caller snapshots and retains mutable inputs before
submission. Reusing the same directory and identical operation rejoins that
request; different inputs require a fresh directory.

A saved handle reconnects status/events/await to the same durable job. Its
coordinator, directory identity and operation digest are checked on each call.
Events persist bounded preparation progress and an explicit truncation notice;
machine results use separate bounded JSON files. await! polls in one coordinator VM. Its deadline or a caller disconnect
leaves the job running.

* Cancellation and recovery

#+begin_src clojure
(jobs/cancel! handle)
(jobs/recover! handle)
(jobs/status! handle)
#+end_src

Cancellation validates the exact request-specific worker argv, PID start
identity and named systemd service membership before signalling. Ambiguous
identity requires recovery and produces no signal. Stopped in-flight work has
an unknown outcome. Recovery reconciles that request's ledger against actual
worker identity; it scans no unrelated jobs. Neither operation releases roots
or authorizes result publication.

Shared Nix realization and request ownership remain distinct: cancelling one
request does not establish that the daemon's shared build has stopped for every
consumer. Operators retain roots until result/consumer ownership is resolved.

* SDK-family production
The coordinator boots independently of the target SDK under construction. The
sdk operation consumes a captured full engine store root and one product name:
sdk, compiler, dependencies or bl-drop. Its fixed recipe reads the lock and
producer implementation from that immutable engine root. Application operations
carry the exact SDK and declared source snapshot; native operations carry the
standalone or explicit workspace-member request.

Current SDK, lifecycle and receiver controls determine production qualification.
A successful job supplies a candidate product for those checks; its status alone
does not establish runtime compatibility or deployment readiness.
